guideposts.label: Dos Hermanas makes its debut as a La Vuelta stage town
guideposts.detail: Dos Hermanas has been the setting of Vuelta a Andalucia stages a handful of times in the 1970s, 1980s and 1990s. guideposts.detail: Enzo Paleni (Groupama-FDJ United), Fredrik Dversnes (Uno-X Mobility) and Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) are 26 seconds ahead of the peloton.

guideposts.label: Last dance for the baroudeurs?
guideposts.detail: Enzo Paleni (Groupama-FDJ United) made it clear yesterday: "Then there’s the time trial, two mountain stages and the finish." The French baroudeur has been one of the most active riders in LaVuelta 26, along with his breakaway companion today, Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH). "One day it’s going to work out", the Spaniard said yesterday.

guideposts.label: 4 minutes
guideposts.detail: At km 16, the peloton are 4'15'' behind the lead duo.

guideposts.label: 6 counter-attackers set off from the bunch
guideposts.detail: They need to close a gap of 4'30'' to Enzo Paleni (Groupama-FDJ United) and Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH).

guideposts.label: The counter-attackers have been reeled in
guideposts.detail: The peloton are now 4'20'' behind the lead duo, who have covered almost 25 kilometres.

guideposts.label: The gap decreases
guideposts.detail: The peloton reach the feed zone (km 30) with a gap of 3'55''.

guideposts.label: Can Cofidis flip the script?
guideposts.detail: Second to Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike) on stages 11 and 16, Bryan Coquard (Cofidis) is looking for an opening to double his tally after winning stage 8 in Xeraco. guideposts.label: 40 kilometres into the stage
guideposts.detail: The gap is now stable at around 3'40''.

guideposts.label: 43.9 km in the first hour
guideposts.detail: That's a strongpace from the lead duo made of Enzo Paleni (Groupama-FDJ United) and Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH).

guideposts.label: The gap is down to 3'10''
guideposts.detail: The peloton are at km 53 with Cofidis and Visma-Lease a Bike at the helm.

guideposts.label: Brennan, inspired by Gaviria and the Maillot Jaune
guideposts.detail: The last sprinter with four stage wins in his debut Grand Tour was Fernando Gaviria in the Giro 2017. The Colombian sprinter then claimed the first Maillot Jaune of the Tour de France 2018. guideposts.label: 3'05'' at km 60
guideposts.detail: The biggest gap recorded so far was 4'30'' at km 18.

guideposts.label: Soon in Alcala de Guadaira, already linked to Seville and Ewan in La Vuelta history
guideposts.detail: Seville left a spectacular mark in the history of La Vuelta when it hosted the Gran Salida in 2010 with a team time trial at night. HTC-Columbia won the stage and Mark Cavendish became the first wearer of La Roja, as the red leader’s jersey was introduced that year, replacing the “maillot de oro” (golden jersey). guideposts.label: Seville, from 1935 to 2024
guideposts.detail: Sevilla was already a stage city in the very first edition of La Vuelta, in 1935. Belgium’s Gustaaf Deloor asserted his dominance on the race as he took the victory while already leading the overall standings. guideposts.detail: Enzo Paleni (Groupala-FDJ United) and Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) are 3'20'' ahead of the peloton.

guideposts.label: The average speed after 2 hours: 43.1 km/h
guideposts.detail: Paleni and Fernandez are setting a strong pace, but the peloton control the gap en route to Seville.

guideposts.label: A gap of 5 minutes
guideposts.detail: The lead duo will soon be halfway through the stage.

guideposts.label: Halfway through the stage
guideposts.detail: Enzo Paleni (Groupama-FDJ United) and Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) havve covered 92.5 km and opened a gap of 5'10''.

I think it’s a very beautiful city. guideposts.label: The tension increases in the bunch
guideposts.detail: As the race enters the final 60 kilometres, the gap falls below 2 minutes and several teams move to the front positions of the peloton.

guideposts.label: The average speed after 3 hours: 43.3 km/h
guideposts.detail: The race is inside the final 55 kilometres. The last gap: 1'40''.

guideposts.label: Into the final 50 kilometres
guideposts.detail: The peloton keep moving closer: 1'25''.

guideposts.detail: Enzo Paleni (Groupama-FDJ United) and Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) have 34 kilometres to go.

guideposts.label: Matthew Brennan wins stage 17 of La Vuelta 26
guideposts.detail: His fifth stage win in his debut Grand Tour - an achievement last recorded in 1979, when Fons de Wolf did it at La Vuelta!
